faq.q: What is the cost difference between the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 in Marbella?
faq.a: There is no cost difference. Both the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 are priced at €749 for 2 hours and €2,299 for 8 hours. This includes skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and VAT. The choice depends on capacity and layout preference, not price.

faq.q: How many passengers can the Astondoa 40 hold?
faq.a: The Astondoa 40 can accommodate up to 9 passengers. It is 12.5 meters long and departs from Puerto Banús. This makes it a good option for smaller groups or those wanting a more intimate experience.

faq.q: How many passengers can the Azimut 39 hold?
faq.a: The Azimut 39 can hold up to 11 passengers. Despite being the same length (12.5m), its layout allows for two extra guests. It also departs from Puerto Banús and is suitable for slightly larger parties.

faq.q: What is included in the charter price for these boats?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden extras—just show up at Puerto Banús and enjoy.

faq.q: Which boat has a flybridge: Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39?
faq.a: The Azimut 39 features a flybridge, providing an upper deck for sunbathing and panoramic views. The Astondoa 40 has a sportier open cockpit layout without a flybridge. Both offer excellent sun exposure and comfort.

faq.q: Where do these boats depart from?
faq.a: Both the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 depart from Puerto Banús in Marbella. From there, you can cruise to nearby spots like Cala del Faro, Cala Cortés, or head towards Estepona for a day on the Costa del Sol.

faq.q: Can I book a half-day or full-day charter?
faq.a: Yes. You can book either 2-hour or 8-hour charters at the fixed rates. For longer or custom durations, contact us via WhatsApp. The 8-hour option gives you plenty of time to explore the coast or anchor for lunch.

faq.q: Are there any additional costs like fuel or tips?
faq.a: No. Fuel is included in the price. Tips for the skipper are not mandatory but appreciated if you enjoy the service. All taxes (IVA) are included, so the price you see is the price you pay.

data.body_html:
When comparing the Astondoa 40 vs Azimut 39 cost in Marbella, the headline is simple: both boats are priced identically at €749 for 2 hours and €2,299 for 8 hours. But cost is only part of the story. These two 12.5-metre vessels from Puerto Banús offer different layouts, capacities, and vibes. Whether you're planning a sunset cruise or a full-day coastal exploration, this breakdown helps you choose the right fit for your group. For a full overview of all options, see our [boat rental Marbella](/).

Cost Comparison: Astondoa 40 vs Azimut 39

Both boats share the same pricing tier (Tier A) in our fleet. There is zero price difference for any duration. Here's the official rate card:

  • 2 hours: €749 per charter (all inclusive)
  • 4 hours: available on request via WhatsApp
  • 8 hours: €2,299 per charter (all inclusive)

These prices include skipper, fuel, drinks (water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava), light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden fees. The choice between the two comes down to passenger count and deck preference, not budget.

Passenger Capacity: Which Boat Fits Your Group?

The Astondoa 40 is licensed for up to 9 passengers, while the Azimut 39 can take 11. If you have a group of 10 or 11, the Azimut 39 is the only choice at this price point. For smaller groups (up to 9), both work equally well. The Azimut's extra capacity comes from its flybridge design, which adds seating without sacrificing interior space. If you need even more capacity, consider our [Mangusta 80](/boats/mangusta-80/) which holds 12 guests.

Deck Layout and Onboard Experience

The Azimut 39 features a flybridge—an upper deck with a second helm station, sun pads, and seating. This is ideal for guests who want panoramic views and a separate sunbathing area. The Astondoa 40 has a sportier open cockpit with a large aft sun pad and a more streamlined profile. Both boats have a bow sunbathing area, a small cabin below, and a wet bar. The choice is between the Azimut's multi-level social space versus the Astondoa's sleek, single-deck elegance.

Typical Itineraries from Puerto Banús

Both boats depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella's iconic marina. Popular routes include cruising west to Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés for swimming in crystal-clear coves, or heading east towards Estepona for a lunch stop. The 8-hour charter allows time to reach Sotogrande or anchor near the Golden Mile. The Azimut's flybridge offers better vantage points for spotting dolphins along the coast. For more ideas, read our [Marbella boat rental guide](/).

Inclusions That Add Value

Every charter includes a professional skipper who handles navigation, mooring, and safety. Fuel is included—no surprises. The drinks package covers water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava, plus light snacks like crisps, nuts, and olives. Insurance and safety equipment (life jackets, first aid, fire extinguisher) are standard. Spanish VAT at 21% is baked into the price. You can bring your own food or arrange catering via WhatsApp. For larger groups, our [Azimut 58 Flybridge](/boats/azimut-58/) offers similar inclusions with more space.

Which Boat Should You Choose?

Choose the Astondoa 40 if you prefer a sportier, more intimate feel with a maximum of 9 guests. Choose the Azimut 39 if you want a flybridge for better views and can use the extra two seats. Both deliver the same value-for-money at identical rates. If your group is larger than 11, explore our fleet of 12-passenger boats like the [Ferretti 94](/boats/ferretti-94/) or [Mangusta 80](/boats/mangusta-80/).

Frequently asked questions

What is the cost difference between the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 in Marbella?

There is no cost difference. Both the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 are priced at €749 for 2 hours and €2,299 for 8 hours. This includes skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and VAT. The choice depends on capacity and layout preference, not price.

How many passengers can the Astondoa 40 hold?

The Astondoa 40 can accommodate up to 9 passengers. It is 12.5 meters long and departs from Puerto Banús. This makes it a good option for smaller groups or those wanting a more intimate experience.

How many passengers can the Azimut 39 hold?

The Azimut 39 can hold up to 11 passengers. Despite being the same length (12.5m), its layout allows for two extra guests. It also departs from Puerto Banús and is suitable for slightly larger parties.

What is included in the charter price for these boats?

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden extras—just show up at Puerto Banús and enjoy.

Which boat has a flybridge: Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39?

The Azimut 39 features a flybridge, providing an upper deck for sunbathing and panoramic views. The Astondoa 40 has a sportier open cockpit layout without a flybridge. Both offer excellent sun exposure and comfort.

Where do these boats depart from?

Both the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 depart from Puerto Banús in Marbella. From there, you can cruise to nearby spots like Cala del Faro, Cala Cortés, or head towards Estepona for a day on the Costa del Sol.

Can I book a half-day or full-day charter?

Yes. You can book either 2-hour or 8-hour charters at the fixed rates. For longer or custom durations, contact us via WhatsApp. The 8-hour option gives you plenty of time to explore the coast or anchor for lunch.

Are there any additional costs like fuel or tips?

No. Fuel is included in the price. Tips for the skipper are not mandatory but appreciated if you enjoy the service. All taxes (IVA) are included, so the price you see is the price you pay.
